written: 2026-09-28, before any run of this check
question: Is the heat flagship A's cell participant hands to the coolant consistent with the cell's own energy balance? The existing checks compare the coupled heat with the coolant's m*dh, i.e. the same number on both sides; no cell-side check existed (BIG 13 review M5).
classification: numerical verification of the cell model's heat bookkeeping (an energy identity of the model), not validation
conditions: the flagship's cell exactly as its coupling path builds it: PyBaMM SPM, Chen2020 via forge_pybamm.parameter_set, isothermal with 'calculate heat source for isothermal models', SOC 0.8, 2.5 A discharge for 3600 s (the normal case's discharge hour), at 300 K and at 313.15 K, fresh cell
identity: Total heating = I * (U_surface - V) + Reversible heating, where U_surface is PyBaMM's 'Surface open-circuit voltage [V]' (heat of mixing from particle concentration gradients is not in PyBaMM's heat source by design)

acceptance.C1: | integral(Total heating) - integral(I*(U_surface - V) + Reversible heating) | <= 1 % of integral(Total heating) over the discharge hour, at both temperatures

reported_not_judged: the heat-of-mixing share integral(I*(U_bulk - U_surface)) / integral(Total heating): heat the model does not generate, a model-form limit of the flagship's heat
the reversible share integral(Reversible heating) / integral(Total heating)
no_change_after_seeing_results: conditions, identity and tolerance are fixed
